claims.text: The as-cast HfMoTaTiZr baseline has a density of 10.21 g cm^-3.
The as-cast HfMoTaTiZr baseline has a room-temperature yield strength of approximately 1600 MPa.
The as-cast HfMoTaTiZr baseline has at least 50% room-temperature ductility.
The as-cast HfMoTaTiZr baseline has excellent fracture toughness.
The as-cast HfMoTaTiZr baseline has a yield strength of approximately 855 MPa at approximately 1000 °C.
The intervention replaces 10 atomic percentage points of Hf with Al while leaving the other elemental fractions unchanged.
Replacing Hf with Al will reduce alloy density by approximately 8–10%.
The Al-modified alloy will retain high configurational entropy.
The Al-modified alloy will preserve a single-phase solid-solution microstructure.
The Al substitution will preserve the solid-solution-strengthening effects of HfMoTaTiZr.
Al lowers average atomic mass, thereby lowering the overall alloy density.
A controlled 10 at% substitution will not significantly alter phase stability.
The modified alloy will have a density near or below 9.5 g cm^-3.
The modified alloy will retain room-temperature yield strength within 10% of 1600 MPa.
The modified alloy will retain at least 50% room-temperature strain to failure.
The modified alloy will retain yield strength at approximately 1000 °C within 10% of 855 MPa.
Al segregation may produce unwanted precipitates that reduce ductility or high-temperature strength.
Mechanical performance will be evaluated under quasi-static loading at room temperature and approximately 1000 °C.
Modified and baseline specimens should be processed using the same casting and heat-treatment protocols.

contradictions.description: An 8–10% reduction from 10.21 g cm^-3 corresponds to approximately 9.39–9.19 g cm^-3, not 9.5 g cm^-3. The rejection rule treats remaining above about 9.5 g cm^-3 as equivalent to failing an 8–10% reduction, although 9.5 g cm^-3 represents only about a 7.0% reduction.
